questions.question: The ‘Servants of India Society’ was the brainchild of which of the following leaders?
questions.solution:
The Servants of India Society was formed in Pune in 1905 by Gopal Krishna Gokhale. Purpose:
  • To unite and train Indians of different ethnicities and religions in welfare work.
  • Gokhale was the political guru of Mahatma Gandhi.

questions.question: ‘Wings of Fire’ is the autobiography of _______.
questions.solution: Wings of Fire is the autobiography of Dr. APJ Abdul Kalam, the 11th President of India (also known as the 'Missile Man of India'). Co-author: Arun Tiwari.

questions.question: The Harshacharita is written in Sanskrit by _________.
questions.solution: Harshacharita is the biography of King Harshavardhana of the Pushyabhuti dynasty, written by his court poet Banabhatta in Sanskrit. Banabhatta also wrote: Kadambari.

questions.question: In the Interim Government formed on 2 September 1946, Liaquat Ali Khan was given the charge of:
questions.solution:
In the Interim Government formed in 1946, Liaquat Ali Khan (representing the Muslim League) was appointed as the Finance Minister. Other portfolios:
  • Jawaharlal Nehru: External Affairs & Commonwealth Relations.
  • Sardar Patel: Home, Information & Broadcasting.
  • Baldev Singh: Defence.

questions.question: The deliberations of the representatives at the Third Round Table Conference was held during the later months of which year?
questions.solution:
The Third Round Table Conference was held in London between November and December 1932. Context:
  • The Indian National Congress did not participate.
  • The outcomes led to the Government of India Act, 1935.

questions.question: Which of the following organisations was founded in Poona, Satara and other towns of Maharashtra that worked against Brahmanical orthodoxy and tried to reform Hinduism?
questions.solution:
The Paramahansa Mandali was founded in 1849 in Bombay by Dadoba Pandurang and Durgaram Mehtaji. Focus:
  • It was a secret society that worked against the caste system and advocated for widow remarriage and education for women.

questions.question: In which of the following years was the Muslim League formed?
questions.solution:
The All India Muslim League was founded in December 1906 in Dacca (now Dhaka). Founders:
  • Nawab Salimullah, Aga Khan III, and Nawab Mohsin-ul-Mulk.
  • The league supported the Partition of Bengal.

questions.question: Who among the following was the successor of Mughal emperor Shahjahan to the throne?
questions.solution:
Aurangzeb emerged victorious in the war of succession among the sons of Shah Jahan. Key Battles:
  • Battle of Dharmat and Battle of Samugarh (1658) against his elder brother Dara Shikoh.

questions.question: Tansen, the music legend was a courtier in which of the following courts before coming to Akbar?
questions.solution: Before joining Akbar's court, Tansen served in the court of King Ramchandra Singh of Rewa (Madhya Pradesh). Note: Akbar sent Jalaluddin Qurchi to bring Tansen to the Mughal court in 1562.

questions.question: When was Khandesh merged into the Mughal empire by Akbar?
questions.solution:
Khandesh was annexed by Akbar in 1601. Significance:
  • This coincided with the fall of the Asirgarh Fort, often called the 'Key to the Deccan'.
  • This was Akbar's last major conquest.

questions.question: Which of the following events took place in 1398?
questions.solution:
The Turko-Mongol conqueror Timur (Tamerlane) invaded India in 1398 during the reign of Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughlaq. Result:
  • Delhi was sacked and devastated, leading to the decline of the Tughlaq dynasty.

questions.question: French possessions in India were restored after the Battle of Wandiwash by the Treaty of ________ signed in the year 1763 between Britain and France.
questions.solution:
The Treaty of Paris (1763) ended the Seven Years' War. Impact on India:
  • French possessions like Pondicherry and Chandernagore were restored but only for trading purposes (no fortification allowed).
  • This effectively ended French political ambitions in India.

questions.question: Tomb of Iltutmish was built in which year?
questions.solution:
The Tomb of Iltutmish was built in 1235 AD near the Qutub Minar complex in Delhi. Architecture:
  • It is known for its beautiful calligraphy and the transition from Indian corbelled arches to true arches.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECT pair of a famous minaret and its construction year in India.
questions.solution:
Charminar was built in 1591 CE (not 1664) by Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah to commemorate the end of a plague. Other Correct dates:
  • Chand Minar (1435), Jhulta Minar (1452), Shaheed Minar (1828).

questions.question: Who among the following Bahmani sultan was noted for cruelty and hence got the title as ‘Zalim’?
questions.solution:
Humayun Shah (Bahmani Sultan) was known as 'Zalim' (the Tyrant) due to his cruel nature. Context:
  • He ruled for a short period (1458–1461) and was succeeded by Nizam Shah.

questions.question: The seven years of war in the 18th century was fought between Britain and ________.
questions.solution: The Seven Years' War (1756–1763) was a global conflict primarily between Britain and France. In India: It was fought as the Third Carnatic War, culminating in the Battle of Wandiwash (1760).

questions.question: The Rajpath was decided to be a permanent venue for the Republic Day parade from which of the following year onwards?
questions.solution: Though the first Republic Day parade was in 1950 (at Irwin Stadium), Rajpath (now Kartavya Path) became the permanent venue starting in 1955. Chief Guest 1955: Malik Ghulam Muhammad (Governor-General of Pakistan).

questions.question: Who made the use of Gun powder common in North India to defeat enemies?
questions.solution:
Babur is credited with making the use of Gunpowder and Artillery (Top-khana) common in North India. Success:
  • He effectively used them in the First Battle of Panipat (1526) to defeat Ibrahim Lodi.

questions.question: Who was the eldest of four sons of Babur?
questions.solution:
Humayun (Nasir-ud-Din Muhammad) was the eldest son of Babur. Siblings:
  • Kamran, Askari, and Hindal.
  • Per Babur's wish, Humayun treated his brothers kindly, which later caused political instability for him.

questions.question: Who among the following was the successor of Muhammad-Bin Tughlaq to the throne?
questions.solution:
Firuz Shah Tughlaq (r. 1351–1388) was the cousin and successor of Muhammad bin Tughlaq. Key reforms:
  • Established new cities (Hissar, Firozabad, Jaunpur).
  • Known for constructing canals for irrigation.

questions.question: With which neighbouring country did India sign the Farakka Treaty in 1996 for sharing of the Ganga Waters and on augmenting its flows?
questions.solution:
The Farakka Treaty was signed in 1996 between India and Bangladesh. Purpose:
  • To share the water of the Ganga River at the Farakka Barrage during the lean season.
  • Valid for a period of 30 years.

questions.question: Vallabhbhai Patel and ________ helped Gandhi in Kheda by organising his tour of the villages and urging the peasants to stand firm against the government.
questions.solution: During the Kheda Satyagraha (1918), Indulal Yajnik accompanied Mahatma Gandhi and Sardar Patel to mobilize peasants against high land taxes during a famine. Result: The government finally agreed to suspend tax collection for that year.

questions.question: Dhruvasena II is related to which of the following ruling dynasties?
questions.solution:
Dhruvasena II (also known as Baladitya) was a ruler of the Maitraka Dynasty of Vallabhi (Gujarat). Historical fact:
  • He was the son-in-law of Harshavardhana.
  • The Chinese traveler Xuanzang visited his court.

questions.question: Which of the following mosques/masjids was built during the reign of Lodi dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
questions.solution: Moth ki Masjid was built in 1505 by Wazir Miya Bhoiya, the Prime Minister of Sikandar Lodi. Style: It is considered the epitome of Lodi style architecture.

questions.question: The Delhi sultan, who succumbed to injuries as a result of his fall from horse was _____.
questions.solution: Qutubuddin Aibak, the founder of the Slave Dynasty, died in 1210 due to a fall from a horse while playing Chaugan (an early form of Polo). Tomb: He is buried in Lahore.
